title: Ông bà chăm cháu · Agree / Disagree
prompt: Some people believe that providing financial support to grandparents who regularly care for grandchildren should be a priority. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: Grandparents often subsidise family childcare through their own time, travel and household spending. I support financial assistance for grandparents who regularly provide childcare, provided accepting the payment never removes their freedom to refuse caring duties.

Recognition can make informal care arrangements more sustainable. Regular childcare can reduce grandparents' paid work or create transport and household expenses. A modest allowance could cover travel and meals for a grandparent providing several days of care. Recognising these expenses can prevent help that appears free to the parents from quietly imposing financial insecurity on the older relative providing it.

Payments may reinforce an expectation that older relatives should sacrifice their own plans. Once an allowance exists, relatives may interpret it as payment for expected availability rather than recognition of voluntary help. Grandparents can then face pressure to reduce their own work, rest or social plans, even where the sum does not cover the full personal cost. Support should be voluntary and preserve access to formal childcare alternatives. Voluntary eligibility and access to formal alternatives reduce pressure to accept caring duties, protecting the grandparent's time, health and plans as well as family income. An allowance should stop when a grandparent chooses to reduce care, without penalising the household through loss of access to nursery places or other ordinary childcare assistance. Covering real expenses can prevent financial hardship among older carers, but this benefit is persuasive only when formal childcare remains available and family consent is genuine.
In conclusion, assistance should recognise the costs of voluntary grandparent care, while preserving alternatives that allow older relatives to protect their health, employment and personal plans.
